bullets.title: AVGO: Raising $70-80B in Debt for AI Infrastructure Expansion
bullets.body: CNBC's David Faber reports Broadcom is seeking to raise $70-80B in debt, up from earlier Bloomberg reports of $60B+. The capital raise appears tied to AI-related growth initiatives including custom ASIC work for Anthropic and others. Separately, internal technical analysis flags AVGO weakness as preferred short expression with semiconductor index 73% above long-term trend.

bullets.title: MRVL: Oppenheimer Raises PT to $300; Google 7-Year LTA Validates Platform
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raises MRVL PT to $300 on AI/networking acceleration, modeling $24B CY28 revenue and $9.71 EPS. A 7-year LTA with Google (up to 59M warrants; potential $120B cumulative revenue through 2033) and MSFT ramp beginning late CY26 anchor the bull case. MRVL reports F2Q on 8/27 with DC segment expected up 17% Q/Q and 44% Y/Y; stock is up 196% YTD and trades at 39x CY27E EPS. Hedgeye also flags MU and MRVL as largest positive S&P contributors recently with renewed bullish TRADE/TREND signals.

bullets.title: NVDA: $109B+ Q3 Guide Needed to Impress; Cloverleaf Investment Confirmed
bullets.body: Mizuho notes NVDA needs to guide $108B+ for Q3 (consensus $107B) to move the stock, with Q2 bogey at $95B vs $92B consensus; buyside growing unimpressed with typical $3B beat cadence. Past 5 earnings have shown flat to -5% next-day reactions. Separately, NVDA made a minority investment in Cloverleaf Infrastructure to accelerate clean-powered AI factory data center development. Risk Range set at $213-$230; Trade/Trend levels $212-$205.

bullets.title: MU: Bounced to Higher High; Technical Setup Improving Into NVDA Earnings
bullets.body: Trader commentary notes MU has bounced and formed a higher high; stop-loss sits below recent discouragement lows. Hedgeye's McCullough flagged MU (alongside MRVL) as largest positive S&P 500 contributors with renewed bullish TRADE/TREND signals. BMO initiates outperform on MU with a $1,300 PT. Separate technical analysis recommends shorts below $890.

bullets.title: TSLA: China Recalls ~2.74M Vehicles; Nevada Robotaxi Permits Approved for 5K Cars
bullets.body: China's market regulator ordered Tesla to recall approximately 2.74M vehicles (figures vary across reports; ~1.96M Model Y and up to 2.98M including Model 3/Y) for emergency door-release safety issues, resolved via software update and warning labels—Tesla's largest-ever China recall. On the positive side, Nevada approved Tesla for 5,000 robotaxi permits (vs. Waymo's 1,000), with TSLA expecting to deploy ~2,500 vehicles within 12 months.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU App Store Fee Cuts Pressure Services; AI Music Labels Launched
bullets.body: Apple is lowering App Store commissions to 26% in the EU and allowing third-party payment processors, reducing its moat and pressuring Services revenue growth. EU concessions set a precedent for further regulatory pressure across business areas. Separately, Apple Music is launching 'Made With AI' labels for songs materially generated by AI (33%+ of monthly submissions are 100% AI-generated), and ChatGPT launched an Apple Messages plugin to draft/send texts.

bullets.title: SPOT: Upsizes Share Repurchase Program by $1.5B to ~$2.2B Total
bullets.body: Spotify's Board approved a $1.5B increase to its share repurchase program, bringing the total authorization to approximately $2.223B.

bullets.title: ORCL: VA Raises Cerner Contract Ceiling by ~$17B to $27B
bullets.body: The VA increased Oracle Health's EHR contract ceiling by ~$17B to nearly $27B, with three optional one-year extensions through May 2031. Only 14 of 164 VA medical centers are live, leaving substantial deployment ahead. Mizuho reiterates Outperform, viewing this as validation of the Cerner turnaround and an accelerant for Oracle SaaS revenue growth alongside OCI.

bullets.title: AMZN: Consolidating Post-Earnings; Top Ackman Holding at 10.5% of Portfolio
bullets.body: GS sales desk notes AMZN has been lower on 19 of 26 sessions but is still up ~5% over the past month; the desk sees limited incremental bear case and describes it as consolidating. Bill Ackman's Q2 portfolio lists AMZN as a 10.5% position (~$2.0B). Separately, MRVL's top customer AMZN is ramping custom AI ASICs over the next several years.

bullets.title: UBER: Technical Repair Above 200-DMA; 12.7% of Ackman Portfolio
bullets.body: GS flags UBER as one of the heavily out-of-favor names showing technical repair above its 200-DMA, up 10 of 14 days recently. Robotaxi survey suggests rideshare platforms like Uber/Lyft are best positioned to scale robotaxi services. Ackman's Q2 portfolio lists UBER as his largest position at 12.7% (~$2.5B).

bullets.title: CRM: More Disliked Than Expected; Approaching Earnings at Jackson Hole Week
bullets.body: GS app software bull/bear debate screened CRM as more disliked than expected. CRM is cited as technically recovering above 200-DMA. Mizuho flags CRM earnings as a key event next week alongside NVDA, WDAY, and CRWD.

bullets.title: GOOGL/Waymo Leads Robotaxi Preference at 65%; TSLA at 13%
bullets.body: A survey of 1,005 U.S. consumers in 12 test cities shows Waymo accounts for 89% of robotaxi trial and 65% of stated preference; Tesla at 25% trial/13% preference. Safety (73%) dominates as the barrier over cost (19%). Robotaxis expected to scale through rideshare platforms rather than standalone services.

bullets.title: RBLX: Metaverse Engagement Down 26.5% YoY; Comp Pressure Easing Into September
bullets.body: Hedgeye reports RBLX metaverse engagement declined 26.5% YoY last week, with August tracking -25.7% YoY through 8/9. Monthly growth in July was +7.4% vs. a 14.7% historical average; Q2 was -20.8% YoY. August marks the last month of tight comparables, suggesting comp pressure will ease into Q3.

bullets.title: META: $1.4T Liability Claim Dismissed; State AGs Estimate ~$200B Exposure
bullets.body: A trial dismissed the $1.4T liability claim against Meta as unreasonable; state attorneys general now estimate approximately $200B in potential liability, a substantial reduction in tail risk.

bullets.title: BABA: Cloud Revenue Miss When Adjusting for T-Head Chip Unit; AI Valuation Questioned
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes BABA's Cloud Intelligence Group missed cloud revenue estimates when adjusting for inclusion of the T-Head chip unit. Restructuring is described as masking underlying weakness; Qwen AI business lacks evidence of loss reduction to justify a premium valuation. Separately, Bloomberg notes Alibaba has competitive advantages in AI agent monetization.

bullets.title: T (AT&T): Cuts Anthropic AI Spending Up to 90% on Open-Source Shift
bullets.body: AT&T is shifting AI workloads to open-source models and cutting spending on Anthropic by up to 90%, according to pre-market sector summaries. This is a notable signal of enterprise AI cost optimization favoring open-source over proprietary LLM vendors.

bullets.title: NTNX: Options Volume Spike 375% Ahead of Aug-26 Earnings; Nutanix-ChronoScale GPU Partnership
bullets.body: NTNX options volume spiked to 5,852 contracts vs. 1,561 average (375% above normal) ahead of its August 26 earnings report. Separately, a Nutanix-ChronoScale partnership adds GPU capacity and AI services, strengthening its AI infrastructure ecosystem positioning.

bullets.title: BMO Initiates Semiconductor Coverage: NVDA $340, AVGO $455, AMD $550, MU $1,300, MRVL $250
bullets.body: BMO Capital Markets analyst Harsh Kumar initiates outperform coverage across the semiconductor space: NVDA at $340, AVGO at $455, AMD at $550, ADI at $430, MRVL at $250, and MU at $1,300. QBTS separately initiated at $35.

bullets.title: COHR/ALAB/STX/LITE: AI High-Flyers Compressing from ~70x to ~40x P/E in 45 Days
bullets.body: GS sales desk notes AI optical/interconnect names COHR, ALAB, LITE, and STX are seeing multiple compression from ~70x to ~40x P/E over the past 45 days despite rising estimates. COHR is up 2.5% in pre-market. The desk views this as valuation normalization, not fundamental deterioration.

bullets.title: TLN: Down 13% YTD on PA Exposure, But Gov. Shapiro Carve-Out Supports FCF Thesis
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes TLN is down 13% YTD on Pennsylvania data center power exposure concerns, but Gov. Shapiro's executive order carve-out for projects with existing utility contracts (ESAs/TSAs) covers meaningful load. PA power prices and sparks have not corrected like Texas post-Batch Zero pause, supporting a high-teens FCF/equity yield thesis a couple years out.
